new_entities.name: Topical tretinoin
new_entities.description: Topically applied tretinoin formulations used for acne or photoaging.

new_entities.name: Clinical photoaging grading
new_entities.description: Clinician-graded or trial-graded signs of photodamaged skin such as fine wrinkling, lentigines, roughness, and overall photoaging severity.

edges.effect_quant: A 48-week randomized placebo-controlled trial of tretinoin emollient cream in 40 patients found significant improvement in global photoaging evaluation and fine wrinkling by 24 weeks. Two modern systematic reviews then concluded that randomized trial evidence consistently shows clinical photoaging benefit, even though formulations and comparators vary.
edges.population: adults with photodamaged facial or forearm skin treated with topical tretinoin over months rather than days
edges.mechanism: Topical tretinoin promotes epidermal turnover and new collagen formation while reducing features of extrinsic photoaging such as fine wrinkling and mottled pigmentation.
edges.summary: Topical tretinoin remains one of the more defensible photoaging interventions. The evidence is not hype-free because trials use varied concentrations and comparators, but the overall direction toward clinical improvement is consistent enough to support a beneficial classification.
edges.caveats: The benefit comes with irritation tradeoffs and requires sustained use, so this is not a quick cosmetic fix. It is also a prescription-strength edge, not proof that over-the-counter vitamin A products behave the same way.
